messages.body_plain:
Hello Ed,

Today I have a very simple question, that I believe is related to rjags.

I've been running a very simple CFA model, and suddenly it tells me that I'm not passing the right object:

"Compiling rjags model...
Error: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors"

If I try to fit the model using runjags or rjags the model runs fine. Do you have any idea if I'm doing something wrong of if the arguments of blavaan function have changed?

I'm attaching the dataset and you'll see my code and session info below. I'll appreciate any help you can give me.

testData <- read.csv("testing.csv", na.string = "NA")

modCFA <- 'tsccAnx =~ tsccAnx1 + tsccAnx2 + tsccAnx3
           tscycAnx =~ tscycAnx1 + tscycAnx2 + tscycAnx3

          tsccDep =~ tsccDep1 + tsccDep2 + tsccDep3
          tscycDep  =~ tscycDep1 + tscycDep2 + tscycDep3

          tsccPTS =~ tsccPTS1 + tsccPTS2 + tsccPTS3

          tscycPTS =~ tscycIntru + tscycAvoid + tscycArousal

          tsccDis =~  tsccDis1 + tsccDis2 + tsccDis3
          tscycDis =~  tscycDis1 + tscycDis2 + tscycDis3

         tsccSC =~ tsccSc1 + tsccSc2 + tsccSc3
         tscycSC =~ tscycSc1 + tscycSc2 + tscycSc3

        tsccAnger =~  tsccAnger1 +  tsccAnger2 +  tsccAnger3
       tscycAnger =~  tscycAnger1 +  tscycAnger2 +  tscycAnger3

'

fitB1 <- bcfa(modCFA,
              data= testData,
              n.chains = 3,
              burnin=25000,
              sample=5000,
              target = "jags",
              bcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
              mcmcfile = TRUE,
              do.fit = TRUE)

Thanks for the example code!

Ed

Esther,

Thanks for the clarification. I just tried this out with your versions of lavaan and blavaan (I had not tried the newest version of lavaan), and it seems to be working for me. Two possibilities come to mind, though I'm not sure whether either will solve the problem:

1. Rstudio sometimes installs packages in a different location than R, and you end up using older versions of packages when you think you are using newer versions. You might check whether this code works in R, outside of Rstudio.

2. You might load blavaan before (instead of) lavaan. That is, instead of

library(lavaan)
library(blavaan)

Try just using

library(blavaan)

which also loads lavaan as a side effect. Let me know!

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Multilevel SEM in blaavan?
messages.body_plain:
Tahani,

Multilevel SEM is not currently possible in blavaan (though it is on the TODO list). Your best bet is to export the jags or stan syntax of a one-level SEM via mcmcfile=TRUE, then edit it to be a multilevel SEM. But this admittedly requires some effort.

Best,
Ed
